newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal, Scotiabank post higher Q2 profits.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal, Scotiabank post higher Q2 profits.

text.p: Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia posted higher second quarter earnings on Tuesday, but disappointed some investors when they did not hand out bigger dividends.
Bank of Montreal, Canada's third largest bank, said earnings rose to C$1.11 ($0.80) per share in the second quarter ended April 30, up from C$0.98 ($0.71) a share in the same period last year.
But profits were down slightly from record earnings of C$1.16 ($0.84) a share in the first quarter of 1997.
Bank of Nova Scotia, the country's fourth largest bank, said second quarter profits jumped to a record C$1.16 ($0.84) per share from C$1.01 ($0.73) in the same period a year ago.
Scotiabank earned C$1.14 ($0.82) a share in the first quarter of 1997.
Analysts said profits at the two banks were in line with market expectations. But the absence of a dividend hike or stock split may have disappointed some investors.
"Both banks either met expectations or slightly exceeded them," said Hugh Brown, analyst with Nesbitt Burns Inc.
"There were no dividend increases and no stock splits and I guess some people were disappointed, but they will come," he said.
Bank of Montreal's stock tumbled C$1.15 to close at C$53.90 on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Bank of Nova Scotia finished up C15 cents at C$58.95, a 52-week high.
Scotiabank said its second quarter was highlighted by a drop in net impaired loans to C$364 million ($263 million) from C$690 million ($499 million) in the second quarter of 1996.
The bank also credited strong performances in retail, commercial, corporate, investment and international banking.

Scotiabank said it recorded a C$118 million (US$85 million) pre-tax gain from the sale of its pension and institutional custody businesses, most of its dealer financial services portfolio, and the bank's stake in Montrusco Associates.

Bank of Montreal said business outside Canada accounted for nearly half of the bank's total earnings in the first six months of 1997. The bank said strong growth in loan volumes, investment banking and its global treasury group contributed to its second quarter results.
In Canada, retail and commercial assets grew as average residential mortgages increased by C$3.1 billion ($2.2 billion) from the prior year to C$29.2 billion ($21 billion).
"Small business loan volumes and personal mortgage business are showing significant growth," Bank of Montreal Chief Executive Matthew Barrett said in a statement.
